rationale:
Ported from s2+data40k/p10 (4.3754 there): Three linked changes, all aimed at letting the model use a faster learning rate safely.

(1) Fix the embedding init scale. xavier_uniform on the 50257×256 token table gives std ≈ 0.0063. On the 128×256 position table it gives std ≈ 0.07, so at init the position signal is about 10× larger than the token signal in the residual stream. Rare tokens get few updates, so their rows stay near that tiny scale for a long time. Because the embedding is tied, these rows are also the output logits, so rare-token logits stay near zero too. I switch to GPT-2 init: N(0, 0.02) for the token table and N(0, 0.01) for positions. That makes token identity the dominant input signal and gives reasonably scaled output logits from step 0.

(2) Add global gradient-norm clipping at 1.0 in before_optimizer_step. The median grad norm is 0.40 and p95 is 0.47, so clipping almost never fires in normal steps. It only caps the 4 observed loss spikes.

(3) Given that safety margin, raise peak lr from 2e-3 to 3e-3 and warmup from 300 to 400 steps. The last lr increase (1.2e-3 → 2e-3) gave about −0.08, and the incumbent is diagnosed "still_improving" at the token budget. A faster effective learning rate should get more out of the fixed number of tokens. Weight decay (0.1, including the embedding) is kept as in the incumbent. With a higher lr, the decay also shrinks weights faster, since AdamW's decay step scales with lr×wd.
